research_notes.text: Visitors highlight the large enclosure, separation by dog size and shade from mature mango trees.
The local guide lists a drinking fountain, shelter, seating and waste bags.
Council maps one off-leash area here. The Boundary Rd Dog Park pin is beside that enclosure.
A DogPack reviewer mentions plenty of shade and seating, an obstacle course and parking across Boundary Road.

places.name: Whites Hill Reserve (Boundary Rd Dog Park)
places.description: Also listed as Boundary Rd Dog Park near Holland Park. Enter the fenced off-leash area from Boundary Road at the south-west corner of Whites Hill Reserve. Separate yards cater for large and small dogs. The enclosure has benches, shade from mature mango trees, drinking water, agility equipment and waste bags. Dogs stay on-leash on the reserve trails.

research_notes.text: A visitor appreciated parking on both sides, public toilets and plenty of covered seating and barbecue space. These observations concern the wider park.
The directory lists shade and water for the park. It does not establish that water is available in the off-leash area itself.

places.name: Glindemann Park
places.address: 1208 Logan Road, Holland Park West QLD 4121
places.description: Glindemann has an unfenced off-leash area. The wider park has shady spots, undercover seating, barbecues and public toilets. A dog-bowl fountain is mapped elsewhere in the park, so plan to bring water into the off-leash area.

research_notes.text: A dog owner reported a fountain in each enclosure, shaded seating in the larger yard and toilets nearby.
Visitors mention friendly owners, separate dog yards and a playground nearby. The guide says weekend mornings can draw a crowd.

places.name: Shaftesbury Street Park
places.description: Separate fenced and double-gated yards cater for big and small dogs. Visitors report a drinking fountain in each yard and shaded seating in the larger one. Toilets and a playground are close by. Weekend mornings can get busy.

research_notes.text: Visitors liked the upgraded small-dog section and the loop around the wider park. Limited seating and a lack of toilets came up in comments.
The guide reports water stations and mature shade, but advises carrying water in case the stations are unavailable.

places.name: Abbeville Street Park
places.address: 41 Abbeville Street, Upper Mount Gravatt QLD 4122
places.description: The fenced area has a separate small-dog section, shade from mature trees and dog water stations. Visitors mention the walking loop around the wider park. A local guide advises bringing water as a backup, and reviewers report limited seating and a lack of toilets.

research_notes.text: The guide reports a drinking bubbler and a double-gated entry, and says bare earth can become muddy after heavy rain.

places.name: Ekibin Park East
places.description: The fenced dog area is on the Victoria Terrace side of the park. A local guide lists a double-gated entrance, shade, seating and a bubbler.

places.name: Wembley Park
places.description: The fenced Coorparoo enclosure has room to run, shade and agility equipment. Council maps a drinking fountain and tap.

research_notes.text: A regular said the fenced yard can get busy and large and small dogs use the same space.
DogPack lists a water fountain, a double-gated entrance and nearby parking.

places.name: Joe Bradfield Centre Park
places.description: The Carina enclosure has a double-gated entrance, a drinking fountain and parking nearby. A regular reports that large and small dogs share the yard and it can fill up at busy times.

places.name: Perth Street Park
places.description: The wider park has shade and separate areas for family recreation and off-leash dogs. Council maps a drinking fountain and dog bowl in the enclosure.

research_notes.text: The Tones Road enclosure listing describes a short uphill walk from parking. Reviews on the listing mention morning sun in the dog area.
A local guide reports a dog bubbler, agility equipment and waste bags at the Tones Road site.

places.name: Ron Woolley Place
places.description: The Tones Road fenced enclosure has a dog bubbler, agility equipment and waste bags. A local listing describes a short uphill walk from the parking area, and visitors mention morning sun in the yard.

research_notes.text: Visitors liked the shade and tidy facilities. Some found parts of the wider park poorly lit at night.

places.name: Woolloongabba Rotary Park
places.description: The park has a fenced off-leash area beside separate family recreation spaces, with shade and open ground. Parts of the wider park can be dark at night.

research_notes.text: The dog park listing describes one shared yard with a bench by the dog facilities.
Council lists new gates, seating and turf works for 1 February to 1 May 2027, with the dog park closed.

places.name: Berkshire Crescent Park
places.description: A single fenced off-leash yard with a bench, water tap and waste bags. Council lists the dog park as closed from 1 February to 1 May 2027 for gate, seating and turf works.

research_notes.text: The dog enclosure listing reports double gates and shaded places to sit.
The wider reserve's reviews also cover family facilities such as the playground.

places.name: Carindale Recreation Reserve
places.description: Enter the large fenced off-leash area from Cadogan Street. Local listings report shaded seating and parking. Council maps a drinking fountain with a dog bowl inside the enclosure.

research_notes.text: Find a Dog Park describes a narrow enclosure with a double-gated entrance and seating among shady trees.

places.name: Vectis Street Park
places.description: This fenced off-leash yard off Scott Street is also listed as Norman Park Off Leash Dog Park. It has seating, shade trees, agility equipment, drinking water and lighting. Dogs of all sizes share the yard.

research_notes.text: The local guide lists seating under a shelter, a water tap and a double-gated entry.

places.name: Salisbury Recreation Reserve
places.description: The fenced off-leash area near Wincott Street and Evans Road has separate large- and small-dog yards, covered seating, drinking water, lighting and agility equipment.

research_notes.text: The guide reports a covered shelter with seating and street parking off Cribb Road.
Council maps a drinking fountain with a dog bowl within the off-leash area.

places.name: Newbury Place Park
places.description: A fenced off-leash area with a separate small-dog yard, covered seating, scattered shade trees, drinking water, lighting and agility equipment.

research_notes.text: The enclosure listing reports bench seating and water for dogs, with parking off Meadowlands Road.
Council lists the off-leash area under Preston Road Park, Carina.

places.name: Preston Road Park
places.description: The dog enclosure is accessible from Meadowlands Road. Its fenced off-leash yards have separate areas for large and small dogs, benches, some tree shade, dog drinking fountains, lighting and agility equipment.

research_notes.text: One visitor liked the coffee and toasted sandwich and found the outdoor area a comfortable place to sit with a large dog.
The guide reports that staff often put out water bowls and may make a puppuccino on request.

places.name: Cafe & Bar on Whites Hill
places.description: The café has dog-friendly outdoor seating beside Whites Hill Reserve, with room for a large dog under the table. A local guide reports water bowls are usually available and staff may make a puppuccino on request. One visitor liked the coffee and toasted sandwich.

research_notes.text: A visitor who brought their dog said staff took good care of the dog. Other reviewers highlight plant-based breakfast options.
The café says pets can join diners in its outdoor areas.

places.name: Little Black Pug
places.description: Dogs are welcome in two outdoor dining areas. Puppuccinos, dog biscuits and meatballs have been listed for pups, while diners mention plant-based breakfast choices. The published café number is for booking by text.

research_notes.text: Reviewers liked the coffee, friendly staff and treats for dogs. Some found the house coffee blend more acidic than they prefer.

places.name: Black Lab Coffee
places.description: This Tarragindi coffee shop welcomes dogs in its outdoor seating area and supports animal rescue. Visitors mention friendly staff, dog treats and good coffee. Some found the house blend on the acidic side.

research_notes.text: A visitor noted that the dog-friendly seating is beside the entry. Reviews also highlight the lookout views.
The booking listing offers outdoor tables designated as dog-friendly.

places.name: Lovewell Café
places.address: 185 Mount Gravatt Outlook Drive, Mount Gravatt QLD 4122
places.description: Lovewell is at Mount Gravatt Lookout and lists bookable dog-friendly tables outside. A visitor placed these tables near the entrance. Reviews commonly mention the views over Brisbane.

research_notes.text: A visitor reported plentiful water for their dog and good shade on a hot day, and liked the breakfast.
The café says leashed dogs can join diners in the garden and that it supplies water bowls.

places.name: MK Bower Cafe
places.description: Leashed dogs can sit with diners in the shaded outdoor garden. The venue supplies water bowls, and a visitor reported plenty of shade and water on a hot day. Diners come for all-day breakfast and brunch.

research_notes.text: The venue confirms dog-friendly outdoor seating. Its review roundup highlights the sheltered garden feel and generous brunch portions.
Visitors mention French toast, chicken waffles and outdoor seating. The guide recommends arriving early on weekends for an outside table.

places.name: The Smug Fig
places.description: The Stones Corner café has dog-friendly outdoor seating in a sheltered, garden-style area. Visitors mention generous brunch portions, French toast and chicken waffles. Outdoor tables can fill up on weekends.

research_notes.text: Review summaries highlight the coffee, friendly service and a welcoming outdoor setting for dogs.
The directory reports that dogs can use a small fenced play area behind the café.

places.name: Snag & Brown
places.description: Dogs are welcome in the outdoor courtyard. A local directory describes a small fenced play area behind the café. Review summaries highlight the coffee, friendly staff and outdoor setting.

research_notes.text: A visitor reported a dog bowl brought to the rear courtyard table and treats for the dogs. They also liked the coffee and prompt service.

places.name: Little Genovese
places.description: Dogs can join diners in the rear outdoor courtyard. A visitor reported that staff brought a water bowl and treats for the dogs, and liked the coffee and prompt service.

research_notes.text: A visitor who brings their dog to cafés said the food for dogs felt particularly well considered.
Tourism Queensland lists puppuccinos and a dedicated dog menu at the astro-turfed courtyard.

places.name: Todd & Pup
places.description: The outdoor courtyard welcomes dogs. Tourism Queensland lists puppuccinos and a dedicated dog menu. A visitor with a dog praised the care put into the food for pups.

research_notes.text: Reviewers liked the courtyard for brunch, dietary choices and treats for dogs. Some reported slower service at busy times.
The venue advertises dog biscuits, a dog menu and pupaccinos in its courtyard garden.

places.name: Sassafras of Paddington
places.description: Dogs can join diners in the courtyard garden, where the café advertises pupaccinos, dog biscuits and a dog menu. Reviewers liked the outdoor brunch setting and dietary options. Some reported slower service at busy times.

research_notes.text: The dining guide describes shaded outdoor seating for people with dogs.
Holland Park News reports the café sells Coopers Cookies dog treats.

places.name: Stomp Espresso
places.description: Coffee and light meals on Holland Road. Dogs can join diners at shaded outdoor tables. Local coverage lists dog biscuits for sale.

research_notes.text: Broadsheet describes a wraparound outdoor area that accommodates dogs and larger groups.

places.name: Deedot Coffee House
places.address: 1/973 Logan Road, Holland Park West QLD 4121
places.description: Specialty coffee and brunch on Logan Road. Dogs can join diners in the large outdoor seating area that wraps around the front.

research_notes.text: The local guide describes a compact outdoor dining area on the shared footpath.
A customer reported complimentary dog treats.

places.name: Deli Dakota
places.address: 30 Badminton Street, Mount Gravatt East QLD 4122
places.description: Specialty coffee and sandwiches with dog-friendly footpath tables. Outdoor seating is limited and close to passing pedestrians.

research_notes.text: BringFido identifies the patio as dog-friendly.
The pet-friendly venue listing reports puppuccinos and handmade dog treats.

places.name: Badminton Brew
places.address: 36 Badminton Street, Mount Gravatt East QLD 4122
places.description: A neighbourhood coffee shop with dog-friendly patio seating. Local listings report puppuccinos and handmade dog treats.

research_notes.text: The café's listing reports outdoor seating and treats for dogs.
The vet practice in the same shopping centre mentions puppuccinos for visiting dogs.

places.name: Ralph & Co
places.description: A Camp Hill Marketplace café with dog-friendly seating. Its listing mentions treats for dogs. The neighbouring vet practice mentions puppuccinos.

research_notes.text: The pet-friendly listing identifies the alfresco area as the place to sit with a dog.

places.name: Rabbit & Co Café
places.description: Corner café for coffee and brunch. Dogs can join diners at the outdoor tables.

park_attribution.changes: Selected nearby records, matched addresses and water facilities, and summarized dog amenities.
